According to Apollonius theorem, 

$AD^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{b^{2} + c^{2} - \dfrac{a2}{4}\right\}$

$⇒ AD = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{2b^{2} + 2c^{2} - a^{2}}$

$∵ \dfrac{AG}{GD} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

$⇒ AG = \dfrac{2}{3}AD = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt{2b^{2} + 2c^{2} - a^{2}}$

Similarly $BG = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt{2c^{2} + 2a^{2} - b^{2}}$

So, $cos\theta = \dfrac{BG^{2} + AG^{2} - AB^{2}}{2\left(BG\right)\left(AG\right)}$, where $\theta = ∠ AGB$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{9}\left(2c^{2} + 2a^{2} - b^{2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{9}\left(2b^{2} + 2c^{2} - a^{2}\right) - c^{2}}{2\left(BG\right)\left(AG\right)}$

Now, as $cot{θ}_{2} = 2cot{θ}_{1}$

$\left[∵ \Delta ADC = \Delta ADB\right]$

$⇒ 2b^{2} + 2a^{2} = 10c^{2}$

options: given any positive real number $\alpha,$ we can choose C and T as above such that ratio $\dfrac{\text{Area} ( C )}{\text{Area} ( T )}$ is greater than $\alpha$
given any positive real number $\alpha$, we can choose C and T as above such that ratio $\dfrac{\text{Area} ( C )}{\text{Area} ( T )}$ is less than $\alpha$

$give any C and T as above, the ratio \dfrac{\text{Area} ( C )}{\text{Area} ( T )}$ is
independent of C and T
there exist real numbers a and b such that for any circle C and triangle T as above, we must have $a < \dfrac{\text{Area} ( C )}{\text{Area} ( T )} < b$
questions.solution:
It is given that circumference of $C$ is $l$ and the perimeter of triangle T is $l .$

$2\pir = l ⇒ r = \dfrac{l}{2\pi}$

Now, as we know that area of triangle will be maximum for given perimeter if it is an equilateral triangle, let the length of side of equilateral triangle is ' a, then
$3a = l ⇒ a = \dfrac{l}{3}$
and area of equilateral triangle is

${A}_{2} = \dfrac{3}{4}a^{2}$

$So,{A}_{2} = \dfrac{3}{4}\left(\dfrac{l2}{9}\right) = \dfrac{l2}{12\sqrt{3}}∵ \dfrac{A1}{A2} = \dfrac{l^{2}4\pi}{l^{2}12\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{\pi} > 1$

since, as we took an equilateral triangle, which has maximum area. But we can take a triangle T such that the ratio $\dfrac{\text{area} ( C )}{\text{area} ( T )}$ is greater than any positive real number $\alpha$.

questions.q: The points $C$ and $D$ on a semicircle with $AB$ as diameter are such that $AC = 1, CD = 2$ and $DB = 3$. Then, the length of $AB$ lies in the interval.
questions.solution:
Let the diameter $AB = x$

$∵ ∠ ACB = \dfrac{π}{2}$

and $∠ ADB = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$∴ BC = \sqrt{x^{2} - 1}$

On applying Ptolemy theorem, we get

$AB \cdot CD + AC \cdot BC = AD \cdot BC$

$⇒ 2x + 3 = \sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\sqrt{x^{2} - 9}$

On squaring both sides, we get

$4x^{2} + 9 + 12x = x^{4} - 10x^{2} + 9$

$⇒ x^{4} - 14x^{2} - 12x = 0$

$⇒ x^{3} - 14x - 12 = 0$

Let $f\left(x\right) = x^{3} - 14x - 12$

$∵ f\left(4\right) = - 4$

$f\left(4. 1\right) = - 0. 479$

$f\left(4. 2\right) = 3288$

$∵ f\left(4. 1\right) \cdot f\left(4. 2\right) < 0$

$⇒ x \in [ 4, 1, 4. 2 )$
